candidate.description: Extract ordinary Q4 range arithmetic unchanged into linearQ4Range. Non-nil executors run serial jobs with stack state, and parallel jobs with executor-owned state plus a lazily initialized reusable callback. Clear borrowed state only after all worker completions. Nil-executor dispatch and wide-sum fallback remain non-reused paths.
candidate.tradeoff: Executor holds an additional Q4 descriptor and callback field. First parallel Q4 use allocates one callback; subsequent ordinary calls are allocation-free. Executor allocation size can increase even for other formats, so control-format bytes must not be assumed unchanged.
candidate.decision: Retain as an allocation-reduction candidate, not a demonstrated wall-clock speedup. Local only; no PR or mainline adoption implied.

correctness.red_green: Before the runtime edit, TestQ4InvocationSteadyAllocation/workers1/rows1 failed with 1.0 allocations. After edit ordinary warmed Q4 calls allocate zero with workers1/2/4 and rows1/2/3/4/5/17.
correctness.reference: Existing blockBaselineLinearQ4Into frozen from 6b94640; preserves the same per-output four-accumulator reduction order. This is an arithmetic oracle, NOT the old invocation timing baseline.
correctness.exact_shapes: 882 combinations: workers1/4 x rows0/1/2/3/4/5/7/8/17 x in1/3/63/64/65/129/513 x out1/2/31/32/33/65/259. Ordinary finite input outputs compared by Float32bits with poisoned outputs and guards.
correctness.lifecycle: Assert descriptor cleared after each call, block all four worker callbacks to verify state survives until join, then verify clearing and subsequent reuse. Four independent owners share immutable inputs/weights under race testing. Wide-sum fallback separately compared bitwise including infinite results; ordinary callback must remain uninitialized on a fresh fallback-only executor.

generation_measurement.protocol: Three baseline/candidate fresh-process blocks, order before-after / after-before / before-after. Each binary runs the identical BenchmarkPostSingleExpGeneration harness with 200ms leaves, 18 format/worker/shape cases. The prior baseline test executable is bound by SHA-256 in the summary. Ratios are ratios of independently calibrated benchmark estimates, NOT request-level matched pairs.
generation_measurement.controls: FP32 and Q8 use unchanged arithmetic. Across conditions their median process ratios range approximately 0.993-1.003. These descriptive controls and fixed format order do not prove absence of small regressions.
generation_measurement.interpretation: Allocation reduction reproduced; timing is approximately neutral. Do not call these tiny negative ratios speedups. The benchmark verifies deterministic completions within each binary, not cross-binary identity.
